findings.location: app/src/main/java/com/example/projectacc/MyAccessibilityService.kt closeNonCvPopup closure decision by service node instead of scheduled id
findings.claim: The delayed close previously required the re-read id to equal the scheduled id, and the mismatch path was a silent continue; parseOrder keeps the last ID node in flatten order, so in app mode where the main window can contain several ID nodes the re-read could differ and the timer would exit without logging or closing (the reported symptom). The close decision now uses the product rule (offer popup present and no Cruz Verde service node) regardless of the parsed id, with a log line when the ids differ. Consequence: a scheduled non-CV offer closes even if the id parse shifted between detection and re-read; a different non-CV offer popup in the same window would also close, which matches the product rule that every non-CV offer is closed unconditionally.

product rule documented in the branch comment: servicio empty means no Cruz Verde node in the flattened tree

findings.claim: The timer lifecycle is now fully instrumented: scheduling outcomes in the branch, timer entry with pending state, per-window re-read details, and timer completion before the pendingCloseId reset. The previous build produced exactly one scheduling log and no further output, which left two indistinguishable hypotheses (timer never fired versus silent no-match exit). These lines resolve the ambiguity on the next device run; they add logcat volume only when a non-CV timer is active and can be downgraded afterwards without behavior change.

findings.claim: When the close click succeeds, lastClosedId is set to the scheduled orderId even if the window that was actually closed reported a different parsed id. This keeps deduplication keyed to the scheduled id, so the re-read popup with a shifted id could later be re-detected and re-scheduled once before being blocked by the service-node rule on its own timer. Risk is one extra timer cycle in the id-shift edge case, not a wrong click; the id-difference log makes it observable.
